analysis.investment_thesis: Aarti Pharmalabs is riding the China+1 API tailwind and CDMO boom with impressive 30.6% net profit CAGR and expanding margins, but a promoter holding below 50% and a sharp debt surge (₹285→₹659 Cr in one year) cloud the conviction story. At 29x P/E with negative FCF in FY25, the price already reflects much of the good news.
key_strengths: Exceptional growth trajectory: Revenue CAGR 20.8%, EBITDA CAGR 33.7%, PAT CAGR 30.6% over 3 years — real operational momentum
Structural tailwind: API + CDMO exposure to China+1 theme and India PLI pharma scheme with diversified therapeutic areas (oncology, CVD, CNS)
Improving operating leverage: EBITDA margins expanding with gross margins at a healthy 51.3%, ROCE at 17.4%
key_risks: Debt surge is alarming: Borrowings nearly doubled to ₹659 Cr in FY25, finance costs up 59% YoY — heavy capex cycle (₹444 Cr in FY25) must yield returns or leverage becomes a problem
Promoter holding at 43.08% is below my 50% threshold — insufficient skin-in-the-game for a high-conviction long-term bet
FCF turned negative (-₹112 Cr in FY25) and cash almost depleted (₹83→₹7 Cr) — capital allocation discipline needs to be proved through the investment cycle
red_flags: Promoter below 50% — watch for any further dilution
Borrowings jumped ₹374 Cr in a single year — if utilization of new capacity is delayed, debt servicing could pressure earnings
Company incorporated only in 2019 as a carve-out — limited independent track record through a full business cycle
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aarti Pharmalabs is a credible beneficiary of India's API export growth story. The numbers tell a genuine operational story — revenue went from ₹1,200 Cr to ₹2,115 Cr in three years, and net profit grew from ₹122 Cr to ₹272 Cr. Margins are expanding, not compressing, which signals pricing power in its niche segments (xanthines, specialty APIs, CDMO contracts). The Aarti group pedigree gives some comfort on promoter quality, even if holding at 43% is below what I like to see.

However, FY25 raises yellow flags I cannot ignore. A ₹444 Cr capex blitz funded largely by debt (borrowings almost doubled) has turned FCF sharply negative and nearly drained the cash balance. At 29.3x P/E and EV/EBITDA of 17.3x, the market is pricing in continued 25%+ growth — execution on this expansion must be near-flawless. ROE at 14.5% is below my 20% benchmark, and until the new capacities are absorbed, return ratios will likely stay suppressed. This is a "show me the returns on capex" story for the next 12-18 months before I'd build a large position.
